name: IPMA: warnings on a timeline (Lisboa)

frame.part: top of the page, no scrolling

capture_note: Requested from incident.archivist@: same address, 1280 x 1600 viewport, top of page. Until then the study page draws the callouts on an empty frame. No image is kept in git.
licence_for_showing_the_screenshot: IPMA: free use for personal or public purposes that are not for profit, with the source named, its logo and a link (imagery.json): a screenshot with "Fonte: IPMA" fits if the site is non-profit (a question open with Dinis).
summary: The primary source for Lisbon: eight hazards against 72 hours, then every warning as a bar with its period and one sentence.

callouts.title: Eight hazards by 72 hours
callouts.does_well: One row per hazard (thunder, sea state, rain, wind, snow, cold, heat, fog), one cell per hour for three days, green to red: when each hazard starts and stops, in one picture.

callouts.title: Days marked under the grid
callouts.does_well: "11 nov", "12 nov", "13 nov" with hour ticks at 00, 06, 12, 18.

callouts.title: Each warning as a bar with its sentence
callouts.does_well: "Vento - Vermelho [11 Nov 12:00 - 11 Nov 21:00]" and under it "Rajadas até 120 km/h, podendo atingir 140 km/h nos locais mais expostos." Hazard, level, period, and what to expect.

callouts.title: Every district with its highest level
callouts.does_well: A list on the right: the district's name and a chip ("Vermelho", "Laranja"); the one shown is marked.

callouts.title: UTC, and the last update
callouts.does_well: "Toda a informação em horas UTC" and "Última atualização: terça, 10 de novembro de 2026 às 21:23".

callouts.title: The criteria, linked
callouts.does_well: "Critérios de emissão": what makes a warning yellow, orange or red.
callouts.fed_by: a link; thresholds for the legend of our strip
